notes: Umbra is a single-page exhibition of twelve generative monochrome studies drawn live on Canvas 2D: interference rings, a halftone field, a flow field, ordered Bayer dithering, a harmonograph, phyllotaxis, marching-squares contours, Rule 30, stacked sine scans, a typographic density field, moire gratings and a halftoned sphere. Each plate is seeded and has two live parameters, a deep link, a PNG export and a pointer luminance readout; the method section adds an interactive tone-quantisation demo. Zero dependencies, no webfonts, no image files, no build step, relative paths throughout. Motion is capped at 30 fps, pauses off-screen and in hidden tabs, and defaults to paused under prefers-reduced-motion. Verified in Chromium at 1000x700: no console errors, only local asset requests, and every control, dialog, keyboard path and hash deep link exercised. The test browser could not produce animation frames (no visible window), so the twelve renderers were additionally run against a software rasteriser to confirm output and coverage, and responsive breakpoints were reviewed in CSS rather than emulated; Firefox and Safari were not available.
